sources.entry: OmniPrompt - Your ultimate GPT companion for seamless access on your Mac

summary.one_liner: OmniPrompt is a native macOS desktop app for quick access to GPT models through the OpenAI API, rather than a webview wrapper around ChatGPT.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes OmniPrompt as a V1 native macOS app focused on fast access to GPT on the Mac, built on the API rather than as a webview around ChatGPT. Listed features are startup on login, auto-filling the prompt with currently selected text, shortcut keys, and quick copy. The author lists planned work (not described as done): a token counter that trims messages near an 8k limit, custom personas switchable on the fly, a saved-messages library, and text-to-speech to fill the prompt. The README also floats a longer-term idea of switching between OpenAI, Bard, Llama, and other services, plus image and video generation, but says this is aspirational. The README does not document installation steps beyond a download link to the latest build, and it does not name specific languages or libraries.
use_cases: quick questions to GPT from the Mac
native desktop client for the OpenAI API
keeping a saved library of AI responses
custom persona prompts for AI chat
launching an AI prompt with a keyboard shortcut
how_to_run: Download the latest build from the link in the README (the README does not give further steps)
notable: Native macOS app using the OpenAI API instead of a webview around ChatGPT
Auto-fills the prompt with selected text
Startup on login and keyboard shortcut support
Planned token counter for the 8k context limit and custom personas
caveats: Described as V1 with a narrow feature set; several items are planned rather than shipped
The feature list has an unfinished empty bullet, and the README gives no setup, requirements or API key instructions
License is not stated in the README
